correctness.rationale: The smoothness discriminant follows from g(x^2), with g(0)=1 and characteristic five. The classical Cartier--Manin formula yields diagonal entries b^2+2a and a^2+2b, so the stable rank equals the number of nonzero entries. The Hasse intersection eliminates to a(a^3-2), with discriminant restriction Delta(a,2a^2)=2(a^3-2)^2 and nonzero gradients. Singular monic cubics of constant one have a unique F_q-rational repeated root r and factor as (u-r)^2(u+r^(-2)), yielding q-1 singular pairs. The 3 cube roots lie over F25 and give t_n=2+(-1)^n. The proof derives all counts and zeta functions; exact code independently reproduces F5,F25,F125 finite samples, not the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: The extra-involution genus-two chart parametrizes a natural bielliptic moduli locus with two elliptic quotient factors. The simultaneous Hasse degeneracy has four transverse solutions but only one remains smooth; the other three are genuine triple-root discriminant collisions. The theorem gives a complete geometric classification of its nonordinary crossing and all-extension arithmetic counts with nontrivial parity. These marked parameter invariants have independent geometric meaning for arithmetic stratification and boundary specialization.
